note: Adapted from the original description of the new species in Sjöstedt's (1926) 'Monographie der Termiten Afrikas. Nachtrag' (in German, with a short Latin diagnosis), published as Calotermes Desneuxi n. sp. and later transferred to Neotermes; the alate is described in most detail, while the soldier and worker descriptions of the original entry are fragmentary in the OCR, so only the alate part is given here. The original labels the alate form 'Imago alata'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate dark brown and glossy above, the pronotum slightly paler and the head slightly darker than the abdominal dorsum; head almost square, the posterior margin arcuate, the anterior margin truncate apart from the mandibles; the area above the eyes and in front of the eyes and ocelli distinctly sculptured; antennae 17 (—19)-segmented, segments 2 and 3 equal in length. Pronotum wider than the head, almost rectangular, sides rounded, posterior margin straight and concave in the middle. Wings distinctly tinged reddish brown, the costa and media dark brown, the media close to the subcosta; submedia indistinct. Compared with C. camerunensis of the same genus, this species has wings 3—3.2 mm wide and 12—12.5 mm long from the scale, the latter species having broader wings and larger ocelli that closely adjoin the compound eyes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate: dark brown and glossy above, the pronotum slightly paler and the head slightly darker than the abdominal dorsum; younger specimens paler, with a yellow-red head and an even paler pronotum; antennae, maxillary palps and legs horny yellow; sternites tinged pale brown and broadening outwards. In the male the upper four tergites are only weakly tinged brown near the posterior margin, tergites 5 and 6 are pale only at the base, the narrow tergite 7 is entirely brown, and tergite 8 forms a brown patch on either side joined at the anterior margin of the tergite; in the female the upper four tergites are pale with a narrower brown border along the posterior margin, while tergite 5 and the enlarged tergite 6 (especially the latter) are brown and pale only at the base. Head (excluding the mandibles) square, the posterior angles rounded, the posterior margin very shallowly arcuate, the anterior margin truncate at the labrum; from there to the occiput slightly longer than the width between the eyes; in lateral view the vertex very flat; the labral area indistinct, narrow and not bulging; the thin membrane at the base of the labrum transversely rectangular and obliquely truncate at the sides; frons flat and slightly concave, with one distinctly larger depression on either side and another shallow depression above them; vertex without a fontanelle; the area in front of the eyes and ocelli concave and distinctly sculptured; labrum covering the mandibles, tongue-shaped, narrowing somewhat squarely (the remainder is broken off in the OCR).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements: wing expanse 26—28 mm, body length with wings 16—17 mm, fore wing length 11.5—12 mm and width 3—3.2 mm. Antennae 17—19-segmented. The type locality and the remaining data are fragmentary in the OCR, and only the measurements given above could be read.
